question: Locate the anchor function for the browser_fingerprint field in the console.log object whose action is fingerprint.scan after selecting the full signal level, selecting the hardware canvas driver, entering the UTC-8 timezone seed, enabling the probe, and clicking #initiateProbeBtn. The same value is also sent in the X-Browser-Fingerprint request header. The anchor function is the first target-specific browser fingerprint value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after delegated-click entry, armed gating, signal collection, field normalization, and projection construction, its own function body constructs the target observable browser fingerprint value rather than merely collecting signalLevel/canvasDriver/timezoneSeed inputs, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, writing to console, or issuing fetch. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, raw input collectors, wrappers, or the final sink. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.

anchor_prompt_addendum.usage: Append the shared general anchor resolution rule and worked example to this task prompt when constructing the final agent prompt.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice. Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function. Must match visible_corpus.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends (exclusive).

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. Must start with function <function_name>( and end with that function's closing brace.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function declaration in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function with balanced braces, not a signature fragment, partial body, or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list of candidate chains.
Do not return the final console sink or the fetch call site.
Do not return a generic DOM reader, browser-signal collector, formatter or router when a more target-specific value constructor is present.
Constrain the observable by both action and field.
The target value is browser_fingerprint and should not be confused with fp_shadow, fp_preview or dataset shadow values.
